title: Evaluation preserves flatness of strict systems
statement: Use the actual coefficient sequence site and evaluation functor of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. A flat module sheaf on the coefficient sequence site evaluates to a flat module sheaf over B_n on the original site, for every level n. Flatness means exactness of the site tensor functor; no flatness of the transition ring maps is assumed.

source.place: Modules on Sites, Tag 08FC, applied to the vertical inclusions of Zheng Construction 4.1.

proof.text: Identify evaluated coefficients and additive sections at U with the original system coefficients and sections at (n,U). These identifications preserve scalar multiplication and vertical restriction. Transfer an arbitrary finite relation to (n,U).

source.place: Modules on Sites, Tag 08FC, applied to the vertical inclusions of Zheng Construction 4.1.

proof.text: Apply the local finite-relation criterion for flatness to obtain a covering sieve and finite factorization witnesses. Pull the sieve back along the vertical inclusion at n. The definition of the coefficient sequence topology says it covers U. Restrict the witnesses to vertical arrows and transport them back by the coefficient and additive identifications. Preservation of finite sums and products proves both witness equations, including empty finite families. The converse relation criterion proves flatness of evaluation.
